newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on LatAm crop weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on LatAm crop weather.

text.p: Prospects for an excellent soybean crop in South America because of nearly ideal weather knocked CBOT soybean futures to a lower close, traders said.
"South America is looking like a garden, but it's early in the season," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Traders said soybean plantings were occurring at a rapid clip in key South American growing areas and the crop has been emerging on schedule.
Consultant Safras e Mercado said Brazil's soybean crop was 72 percent seeded as of November 28, above the 67 percent pace a year ago and ahead of the 70 percent average pace.
Fund selling led the way down with the market also weakened by follow through from Friday's lower close.
Prudential Securities sold 2.5 million bushels of January, Refco Inc sold three million January and Rand Financial sold 2.5 million January, traders said.

Commercial buying underpinned the market with Cargill Inc purchasing two million January, Term Commodities bought 1.2 million January and ADM Investor Services bought three million March, traders said.
Soybeans closed 6-1/2 to 9-1/4 cents lower, with January down 9-1/4 at $7.03-1/2 a bushel.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 48,000 contracts, above the 28,227 traded Friday.
In soybean options, Refco Inc sold 300 March $7.00 calls at 19 cents and Rosenthal Collins sold 200 January $7.25 calls at 2-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, above the 9,402 traded Friday.
